activity_templates.learning_objective: Identify the purpose of cardiovascular follow-up and formulate a question for the care team about the participant's own follow-up.
reflection_prompts: In your own words, what is the main reason for the follow-up described in this resource?
What would you like your care team to explain about your own follow-up?
steps: Introduce the topic using the participant's stated question and identified support need.
Offer a suitable reviewed resource in the participant's language and explain its access conditions.
Invite the participant to explain the main message in their own words and identify any unclear information.
Help the participant prepare a question for their care team; personal monitoring decisions remain with the care team.
activity_templates.title: Understanding cardiovascular follow-up

activity_templates.learning_objective: Identify one practical nutrition or activity question or action relevant to the participant's interests and circumstances.
reflection_prompts: Which idea from the resource would you like to explore?
What support or advice would you need before trying it?
steps: Ask whether the participant wants information about food choices or physical activity.
Select a resource matching that topic, the identified support need and the participant's preferences.
Invite the participant to identify one manageable idea and any barriers or questions.
Distinguish general educational information from an individual dietary or exercise prescription.
activity_templates.title: Making manageable everyday health choices

activity_templates.learning_objective: Recognise an information or support need concerning life after treatment and identify a suitable source of support.
reflection_prompts: Which part of this information feels relevant to your situation?
Who could you talk to, or what further information would help?
steps: Ask which aspect of adjustment the participant wishes to discuss, without inferring a literacy need from emotional distress alone.
Offer a reviewed resource matching the recorded need, topic and language.
Invite reflection on what feels relevant and what remains unclear.
Identify a person or service the participant may choose to approach; follow the avatar's operational support and escalation arrangements.
activity_templates.title: Adjusting to life after treatment

records.applicability_notes: General oncology patient information, updated 2024; not specifically developed for AYA survivors. Covers cardiovascular risks, monitoring and prevention before, during and after treatment. Suitable as background education, with exercise, medication and surveillance advice interpreted in the participant’s clinical context.
records.description: Two-page illustrated patient information sheet explaining cardiovascular complications of cancer treatment, assessment and monitoring before, during and after treatment, and practical measures to support cardiovascular health.
records.title: Ficha del paciente: Cardio-oncología

records.applicability_notes: General oncology patient resource, not AYA-specific. Introduces exercise benefits and directs readers towards clinical assessment and suitable programmes. Does not provide an individual exercise prescription.
records.description: Patient infographic introducing exercise in cancer care and encouraging discussion with the oncology team about individually appropriate activity and access to exercise programmes.
records.title: Infografía para pacientes: ejercicio físico y cáncer

records.applicability_notes: General oncology resource, not AYA-specific. Relevant to exercise during treatment and survivorship. Includes situations requiring clinical assessment and adaptation of activity.
records.description: Practical guidance on staying active during and after cancer treatment, covering exercise benefits, activity types, gradual progression, safety considerations and everyday strategies for reducing sedentary time.
records.provider: Fundación Jiménez Díaz – Comprehensive Cancer Center
records.title: Mantenerse activo

records.applicability_notes: General oncology information, not AYA-specific. Includes general dietary targets and advice concerning supplements and reduced immunity; suitability depends on individual nutritional and treatment needs.
records.description: Guidance on balanced eating after a cancer diagnosis, including gradual dietary changes, weight management, food safety, supplements and common nutrition misconceptions.
records.provider: Fundación Jiménez Díaz – Comprehensive Cancer Center
records.title: Alimentación saludable

records.applicability_notes: General survivorship resource, not AYA-specific. Educational content can support adjustment after treatment. References to Kālida courses and services require separate confirmation of availability and eligibility.
records.description: Information on emotional adjustment after cancer treatment, including uncertainty, confidence, changing identity, everyday coping strategies and when to seek additional support.
records.title: ¿Y después del cáncer, qué?

records.applicability_notes: General oncology resource, not AYA-specific. Provides educational coping guidance rather than a psychological treatment programme. Confirm access separately before signposting to the advertised courses.
records.description: Explains stress associated with cancer and presents eight practical strategies for managing daily demands, supporting emotional wellbeing and seeking help from others.
records.title: 8 consejos para gestionar el estrés cuando convives con el cáncer

records.applicability_notes: General oncology overview, not AYA-specific. Provides introductory information and signposting; detailed relationship guidance is contained in separate linked pages.
records.description: Introduces the effects of cancer on relationships and communication, with links to guidance on partners, children, friends and living alone.
records.title: Cáncer y relaciones sociales

records.applicability_notes: Primarily a caregiver-support overview and signposting page. Not specific to caregivers of AYA survivors. Confirm eligibility and availability before recommending provider services.
records.description: Introduces caregivers’ emotional and practical support needs, with links to guidance for adult and young carers and people experiencing bereavement.
records.title: Apoyo a los cuidadores

records.applicability_notes: General oncology article, not AYA-specific. Relevant to identity transitions and adjustment; reflective educational support rather than a structured psychological intervention.
records.description: Explores changes in identity, self-image, roles and priorities associated with cancer, with practical reflection prompts for understanding and adapting to these changes.
records.title: Identidad y cáncer: cómo la enfermedad puede cambiar la percepción de quién eres

records.applicability_notes: General oncology information, with some childhood-treatment context. Includes emergency and service information that requires local interpretation when used across pilots.
records.description: Explains how cancer treatments can affect heart health, including symptoms, cardiovascular assessments, long-term monitoring and practical measures to support cardiovascular wellbeing.
records.title: Heart health and cancer

records.applicability_notes: Particularly relevant to survivors treated as children, teenagers or young adults. Primarily concerns late effects and follow-up. Treatment-specific monitoring and exercise advice require individual clinical interpretation.
records.description: Explains potential heart problems following cancer treatment in young people, including relevant treatment exposures, symptoms to report, follow-up tests and measures to support heart health.
records.title: Late Effects: Heart Problems

records.applicability_notes: Youth-focused collection including post-treatment mental health, coping techniques, professional support and family support. Annotations describe the collection’s advertised coverage; individual resources require separate review when selected for use.
records.description: Collection of mental-health information for young people affected by cancer, covering anxiety, coping strategies, psychological support, asking for help and support from family and friends, alongside personal experiences.
records.title: Cancer and mental health information

records.applicability_notes: Youth-focused survivorship guidance. Includes UK-specific employment, education and support references whose applicability varies between pilots. Content can be viewed in 134 different languages.
records.description: Practical guidance for young people adjusting to life after cancer treatment, covering relationships, identity, work or education, ongoing effects, emotional recovery and fear of relapse.
records.title: Getting Back to Normal After Treatment Ends

records.applicability_notes: Youth-focused survivorship guidance addressing relationship adjustment and communication. Includes discussing treatment-related fertility effects with a partner, rather than detailed fertility guidance.
records.description: Guidance for young people navigating relationships after cancer treatment, including family dynamics, friendships, romantic relationships, independence and communicating personal needs and concerns.
records.title: Relationships after cancer treatment

records.applicability_notes: Designed for people in their 20s, 30s and 40s during and after treatment, including people living with cancer long-term. Uses short sections, reduced text and imagery to accommodate fatigue and reading difficulties. Full-guide access requires name and email registration.
records.description: Illustrated nutrition guide for people living with and beyond cancer, supporting informed food choices, understanding conflicting dietary advice and managing eating difficulties through practical guidance and recipes.
records.title: Overwhelmed by diet and cancer advice? You’re not alone

records.applicability_notes: Primarily signposting rather than detailed educational guidance. Includes UK-specific services, rights and eligibility criteria. Young carers are a separate audience from young people diagnosed with cancer.
records.description: Information and signposting to age-appropriate cancer support for teenagers, young adults and young carers, including practical, emotional, financial and peer-support services.
records.title: Teenagers and young adults affected by cancer

records.applicability_notes: Draws substantially on breast-cancer and treatment experiences, rather than being a dedicated AYA or post-treatment guide. Review relevance of each intended section; distinguish everyday coping tips from treatment-specific symptom advice. Not every topic in the full guide applies to every survivor.
records.description: Practical tips on daily life with cancer, including emotional wellbeing, fatigue, sleep, common treatment effects, sexuality, exercise, food and support from family and friends.
records.provider: Laço (publication hosted by iMM–Laço); drawing on contributions from women with breast-cancer experience
records.title: Dicas para quem vive com cancro

records.applicability_notes: General oncology guide, not AYA-specific. Includes malnutrition and symptom-management advice for active treatment that should not be applied indiscriminately to well survivors. For post-treatment users, prioritise the relevant section and their current nutritional needs. Dietary supplements and individual dietary treatment require professional advice.
records.description: Guide explaining nutrition during and after cancer treatment, food-related myths, symptoms affecting intake, when to seek nutritional support and practical dietary adjustments, with a dedicated post-treatment section.
records.provider: Associação de Investigação de Cuidados de Suporte em Oncologia (AICSO); Andreia Capela, Luciana Teixeira, Elsa Madureira and Sara Torcato Parreira
records.title: Guia de Alimentação na Pessoa com Cancro

records.applicability_notes: Broad adult survivorship guide; not specifically developed for AYA survivors. Because of its length, direct users to relevant sections (e.g., fertility, work reintegration, and emotional wellbeing).
records.description: Patient guide to life after initial cancer treatment, covering follow-up, late effects including cardiovascular problems, healthy living, emotional adjustment, relationships, support services and personal care records.
records.provider: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO); European Cancer Patient Coalition (ECPC); developed in collaboration with the International Psycho-Oncology Society (IPOS)
records.title: Survivorship: ESMO-Patientenratgeber

records.applicability_notes: Broad adult survivorship guide; not specifically developed for AYA survivors. Because of its length, direct users to relevant sections (e.g., fertility, work reintegration, and emotional wellbeing).
records.description: Patient guide to life after initial cancer treatment, covering follow-up, late effects including cardiovascular problems, healthy living, emotional adjustment, relationships, support services and personal care records.
records.provider: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO); European Cancer Patient Coalition (ECPC); developed in collaboration with the International Psycho-Oncology Society (IPOS)
records.title: Sopravvivenza: Guida ESMO per il Paziente

records.applicability_notes: Broad adult survivorship guide; not specifically developed for AYA survivors. Because of its length, direct users to relevant sections (e.g., fertility, work reintegration, and emotional wellbeing).
records.description: Patient guide to life after initial cancer treatment, covering follow-up, late effects including cardiovascular problems, healthy living, emotional adjustment, relationships, support services and personal care records.
records.provider: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO); European Cancer Patient Coalition (ECPC); developed in collaboration with the International Psycho-Oncology Society (IPOS)
records.title: Przebycie choroby nowotworowej: Poradnik dla pacjentów ESMO-ECPC

records.applicability_notes: General oncology article, not AYA-specific. Suitable as an introduction to sexual wellbeing and communication, rather than a fertility-treatment guide. The existing broad topics describe follow-up and emotional context. Confirm suitability for the participant’s age and clinical context.
records.description: Short article on the effects of cancer and treatment on intimacy, body image and sexual wellbeing, including communication about needs, fertility considerations and seeking specialist advice.
records.provider: Narodowy Portal Onkologiczny / Narodowy Instytut Onkologii; content oversight: Dr Maciej Kawecki
records.title: Jak dbać o seksualność w obliczu raka?

records.applicability_notes: Broad survivorship guide rather than an AYA-specific publication. Signpost relevant sections of the 52-page document. Check current clinical and local service applicability before approval. Translation permission stated by this publisher does not establish permission for MAYA to reproduce, adapt or ingest the Polish text.
records.description: Post-treatment guide addressing follow-up care, persistent symptoms, body image and intimacy, emotional adjustment, family and work relationships, support and relaxation.
records.provider: PRIMOPRO; Fundacja Tam i z Powrotem / Program Edukacji Onkologicznej; Polish translation and adaptation of a National Cancer Institute guide
records.title: Życie po nowotworze: Poradnik dla osób po przebytej chorobie

records.applicability_notes: Written for adult cancer survivors and their families/caregivers rather than specifically for AYA survivors. Assess suitability for adult AYAs (18-39) and use with younger adolescents (15-17) separately. Personal treatment, exercise, medication, and surveillance decisions remain with the clinical care team.
records.description: Guide for people who have completed cancer treatment, addressing recovery, ongoing symptoms, emotional and social wellbeing, healthy living and continuing health surveillance.
records.provider: Associação Enfermagem Oncológica Portuguesa (AEOP); Ana Cristina Ferreira and colleagues
records.title: (Sobre)viver ao cancro: Guia de apoio

records.applicability_notes: Relevant across the cancer journey and to carers. Builds source-appraisal and privacy awareness. Some information about services or legal context is specific to Germany.
records.description: Two-page leaflet explaining how to assess online cancer information, check sources and authorship, interpret social-media and AI-generated content, and limit disclosure of personal information.
records.title: Krebs im Internet: So finden Sie gute Informationen

records.applicability_notes: General online health-information appraisal with cancer context; applicable before, during and after treatment.
records.description: Short article explaining how to evaluate online health information by checking the responsible organisation, purpose, funding, expertise, evidence sources and update date.
records.provider: Fondazione AIRC per la Ricerca sul Cancro
records.title: Istruzioni per una navigazione sicura

records.applicability_notes: Relevant to participants who smoke and want cessation support, including after cancer treatment. Not specifically designed for AYA survivors. Medication, prescription-app and treatment choices require appropriate professional advice; check local service applicability.
records.description: Article explaining smoking-cessation approaches, the evidence supporting different methods, practical behaviour-change strategies and sources of professional support.
records.title: Schluss mit Rauchen: Welche Methoden funktionieren?

records.applicability_notes: Particularly relevant to survivors treated in childhood or adolescence and their families. An introductory overview with onward links; approval of this page does not extend to every linked resource.
records.description: Introduction to follow-up after cancer treatment in childhood or adolescence, explaining its purpose, late effects, rehabilitation and continued support for survivors and families.
records.provider: Kinderkrebsinfo / GPOH; Maria Yiallouros and Dr Gesche Riabowol (née Tallen)
records.title: Nachsorge

records.applicability_notes: Directly developed for adolescents (from age 14–16) and young adults (around age 18) transitioning from paediatric to adult oncology care. Applies specifically to AYA survivors of childhood or adolescent cancers rather than those diagnosed in adult care settings. Clinic listings and care pathways are specific to Germany.
records.description: Explanation of the transition from paediatric to adult healthcare, including continuity of follow-up, preparation, growing independence, care planning and possible sources of support.
records.provider: Kinderkrebsinfo / GPOH; Dr Hannah Schmidt and Dr Ingo Menrath; editor: Maria Yiallouros
records.title: Transition - Der Übergang von der Kinder- und Jugendmedizin in die Erwachsenenmedizin

records.applicability_notes: Intended for survivors of childhood, adolescent and young-adult cancer. Lifestyle guidance is general and may require adaptation to treatment-related limitations and the individual care plan.
records.description: Survivor-oriented summary explaining health-promoting behaviours after childhood, adolescent or young-adult cancer, including activity, diet, avoiding smoking and discussing suitable lifestyle changes with professionals.
records.provider: PanCare PLAIN Information Group; Italian PLAIN summary
records.title: Promozione della salute

records.applicability_notes: Particularly relevant to longer-term survivors treated at younger ages. Educational support rather than diagnosis or psychological treatment. Review local professional-support and urgent-help signposting before delivery; external contacts linked by the page are not validated by this metadata proposal.
records.description: Summary of mental-health concerns after childhood, adolescent or young-adult cancer, explaining possible signs, maintaining wellbeing, follow-up and routes to professional support.
records.provider: PanCare PLAIN Information Group; Italian PLAIN summary
records.title: Problemi di salute mentale
